- path: test_perf_sweep_ts.bat
  content: |
      @echo off
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      rem -ts / device-order sweep for the 27B model, 20k context only.
      rem
      rem   phase 1: MTP draft on Vulkan0, both device orders, Vulkan1 share 100..85
      rem   phase 2: MTP draft on Vulkan1 (frees Vulkan0 VRAM), Vulkan1 share 100/90/85
      rem   phase 3: no MTP at all, Vulkan0 share 15/25/30/35 (no draft VRAM cost)
      rem
      rem b = ub in {1536, 2048} (phase 1), 2048 only for phases 2-3
      rem -ot ".*=CPU" is kept everywhere (host buft of the first -dev device)
      rem
      rem logs: prompts_perf\sweep_ts\<tag>_b<B>.log
      rem summary CSV: prompts_perf\sweep_ts\summary.txt
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      setlocal enabledelayedexpansion
      taskkill /F /IM llama-server.exe /T >nul 2>&1
      ping -n 9 127.0.0.1 >nul
      
      set BIN=D:\shared\project\llama.cpp\build\bin
      set M=D:\shared\ai-models\Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf
      set PDIR=D:\shared\project\llama.cpp\prompts_perf
      set OUT=%PDIR%\sweep_ts
      if not exist "%OUT%" mkdir "%OUT%"
      set SUM=%OUT%\summary.txt
      echo tag,dev_order,ts,spec_dev,b,ub,prompt_tps,gen_tps > "%SUM%"
      
      set C=20000
      
      rem base: same as optimal.bat / test_perf_sweep_mtp.bat, -dev and -ts added per run
      set COMMON=-m %M% -ngl 99 -ot ".*=CPU" --load-mode none --pp-dev Vulkan0 ^
       -fa on -ctk q4_1 -ctv q4_1 -t 6 -tb 6 -n 4 --temp 0 -st -lv 5
      
      set SPEC0=--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-type-k q4_1 --spec-draft-type-v q4_1 --spec-draft-n-max 3 --spec-draft-device Vulkan0
      set SPEC1=--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-type-k q4_1 --spec-draft-type-v q4_1 --spec-draft-n-max 3 --spec-draft-device Vulkan1
      
      echo === phase 1: MTP on Vulkan0, device order A = Vulkan1 first, B = Vulkan0 first ===
      for %%B in (1536 2048) do (
          for %%F in (0 5 10 15) do (
              set /a R=100-%%F
              call :run A!R! "Vulkan1,Vulkan0" !R!,%%F Vulkan0 %%B "%SPEC0%"
          )
      )
      for %%B in (1536 2048) do (
          for %%F in (0 5 10 15) do (
              set /a R=100-%%F
              call :run B!R! "Vulkan0,Vulkan1" %%F,!R! Vulkan0 %%B "%SPEC0%"
          )
      )
      
      echo === phase 2: MTP on Vulkan1 ===
      for %%F in (0 10 15) do (
          set /a R=100-%%F
          call :run S1_!R! "Vulkan1,Vulkan0" !R!,%%F Vulkan1 2048 "%SPEC1%"
      )
      
      echo === phase 3: no MTP, more weights on Vulkan0 ===
      for %%F in (15 25 30 35) do (
          set /a R=100-%%F
          call :run NM_!R! "Vulkan1,Vulkan0" !R!,%%F none 2048 ""
      )
      
      echo.
      echo === sweep done, summary:
      type "%SUM%"
      goto :eof
      
      :run
      set TAG=%~1
      set DEV=%~2
      set TS=%~3
      set SPECDEV=%~4
      set B=%~5
      set SPEC=%~6
      set LOG=%OUT%\%TAG%_b%B%.log
      echo ============================================================
      echo %TAG% dev=%DEV% ts=%TS% spec_dev=%SPECDEV% b=%B% ub=%B% c=%C%
      taskkill /F /IM llama-server.exe /T >nul 2>&1
      ping -n 6 127.0.0.1 >nul
      "%BIN%\llama-cli.exe" %COMMON% -dev %DEV% -ts %TS% %SPEC% -c %C% -b %B% -ub %B% -f "%PDIR%\prompt_%C%.txt" > "%LOG%" 2>&1
      echo exit=%ERRORLEVEL%
      findstr /C:"Prompt: " "%LOG%"
      set V0=
      for /f "delims=" %%l in ('findstr /C:"Vulkan0 (RTX" "%LOG%"') do set V0=%%l
      echo !V0!
      for /f "tokens=3,7" %%a in ('findstr /C:"Prompt: " "%LOG%"') do (
          echo %TAG%,%DEV%,%TS%,%SPECDEV%,%B%,%B%,%%a,%%b >> "%SUM%"
          echo %TAG%,%TS%,%%a,%%b
      )
      findstr /C:"offloaded" "%LOG%"
      goto :eof
      
  referencedBy: {}
- path: test_perf_sweep_cuda.bat
  content: |
      @echo off
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      rem b/ub sweep, same context sizes as test_perf_sweep.bat, for the CUDA0 setup:
      rem   model  : IQ3_XXS\Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS (2-part gguf)
      rem   device : CUDA0, lazy-mode on, fitt 800MB, load-mode none
      rem   MTP    : draft-mtp, q4_1 draft KV, n-max 3
      rem   KV     : q4_1 + FA
      rem Context sizes: 5k 10k 20k 30k 45k 60k (prompt files in prompts_perf\)
      rem b = ub in {512, 1024, 2048, 4096}
      rem
      rem Each run logs to prompts_perf\sweep_cuda\C<C>_b<B>_ub<U>.log
      rem Summary CSV (C, b, ub, prompt t/s, generation t/s) ->
      rem prompts_perf\sweep_cuda\summary.txt
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      setlocal
      taskkill /F /IM llama-server.exe /T >nul 2>&1
      ping -n 9 127.0.0.1 >nul
      
      set BIN=D:\shared\project\llama.cpp\build\bin
      set M=D:\shared\ai-models\IQ3_XXS\Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00002.gguf
      set PDIR=D:\shared\project\llama.cpp\prompts_perf
      set OUT=%PDIR%\sweep_cuda
      if not exist "%OUT%" mkdir "%OUT%"
      set SUM=%OUT%\summary.txt
      echo C,b,ub,prompt_tps,gen_tps > "%SUM%"
      
      rem user's spec: CUDA0, lazy on, fitt 800MB, MTP draft on q4_1, q4_1 KV + FA
      set COMMON=-m %M% -dev CUDA0 --lazy on -fitt 800MB --load-mode none ^
       --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-type-k q4_1 --spec-draft-type-v q4_1 --spec-draft-n-max 3 ^
       -fa on -ctk q4_1 -ctv q4_1 -t 6 -tb 6 -np 1 --cache-ram 0 ^
       --chat-template-file "D:\shared\ai-models\chat_template.jinja" --chat-template-kwargs "{\"preserve_thinking\":true,\"reasoning_effort\":\"medium\"}" ^
       --reasoning on --reasoning-format deepseek --temp 0.3 --min-p 0.05 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 40 ^
       -n 4 -lv 4
      
      for %%B in (512 1024 2048 3072 4096) do (
      	for %%C in (5000 15000 30000 45000 60000) do (
      		call :run %%C %%B %%B
          )
      )
      
      echo.
      echo === sweep done, summary:
      type "%SUM%"
      goto :eof
      
      :run
      set C=%~1
      set B=%~2
      set U=%~3
      set LOG=%OUT%\C%C%_b%B%_ub%U%.log
      echo ============================================================
      echo C=%C% b=%B% ub=%U%
      rem kill the model server before EVERY run; the router restarts but stays idle
      rem as long as no request hits port 11434 during the measurement
      taskkill /F /IM llama-server.exe /T >nul 2>&1
      ping -n 6 127.0.0.1 >nul
      "%BIN%\llama-cli.exe" %COMMON% -c %C% -b %B% -ub %U% -f "%PDIR%\prompt_%C%.txt" > "%LOG%" 2>&1
      echo exit=%ERRORLEVEL%
      findstr /C:"Prompt: " "%LOG%"
      rem parse "[ Prompt: 122.0 t/s | Generation: 3.4 t/s ]"
      for /f "tokens=3,7" %%a in ('findstr /C:"Prompt: " "%LOG%"') do (
          echo %C%,%B%,%U%,%%a,%%b >> "%SUM%"
          echo %C%,%B%,%U%,%%a,%%b
      )
      goto :eof

- path: test_perf_sweep.bat
  content: |
      @echo off
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      rem b/ub sweep for the pp-dev feature (per-device host buft + --pp-dev Vulkan0)
      rem Model: Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL
      rem Context sizes: 5k 10k 20k 30k 45k 60k (prompt files in prompts_perf\)
      rem b = ub in {512, 1024, 2048, 4096}
      rem
      rem Each run logs to prompts_perf\sweep\C<C>_b<B>_ub<U>.log
      rem Summary lines (C, b, ub, prompt t/s, generation t/s) go to
      rem prompts_perf\sweep\summary.txt and are printed to the console.
      rem
      rem Total: 6 x 4 = 24 runs. The 60k runs take ~10 min each.
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      setlocal
      taskkill /F /IM llama-server.exe /T >nul 2>&1
      ping -n 9 127.0.0.1 >nul
      
      set BIN=D:\shared\project\llama.cpp\build\bin
      set M=D:\shared\ai-models\Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf
      set PDIR=D:\shared\project\llama.cpp\prompts_perf
      set OUT=%PDIR%\sweep
      if not exist "%OUT%" mkdir "%OUT%"
      set SUM=%OUT%\summary.txt
      echo C,b,ub,prompt_tps,gen_tps > "%SUM%"
      
      rem latest feature params: weights in Vulkan1_Host (zero-copy decode),
      rem prefill weight ops on Vulkan0 via --pp-dev, q4_1 KV + FA
      set COMMON=-m %M% -dev Vulkan1 -ngl 99 -ot ".*=CPU" --load-mode none --pp-dev Vulkan0 -fa on -ctk q4_1 -ctv q4_1 -t 6 -tb 6 -n 4 --temp 0 -st -lv 5
      
      for %%C in (5000 10000 20000 30000 45000 60000) do (
          for %%B in (512 1024 2048 4096) do (
              call :run %%C %%B %%B
          )
      )
      
      echo.
      echo === sweep done, summary:
      type "%SUM%"
      goto :eof
      
      :run
      set C=%~1
      set B=%~2
      set U=%~3
      set LOG=%OUT%\C%C%_b%B%_ub%U%.log
      echo ============================================================
      echo C=%C% b=%B% ub=%U%
      rem kill the routing server before EVERY run: its restart loop brings it back and
      rem assistant traffic keeps the backend loaded, which contends for UMA DRAM
      taskkill /F /IM llama-server.exe /T >nul 2>&1
      ping -n 6 127.0.0.1 >nul
      "%BIN%\llama-cli.exe" %COMMON% -c %C% -b %B% -ub %U% -f "%PDIR%\prompt_%C%.txt" > "%LOG%" 2>&1
      echo exit=%ERRORLEVEL%
      findstr /C:"Prompt: " "%LOG%"
      rem parse "[ Prompt: 122.0 t/s | Generation: 3.4 t/s ]"
      for /f "tokens=3,7" %%a in ('findstr /C:"Prompt: " "%LOG%"') do (
          echo %C%,%B%,%U%,%%a,%%b >> "%SUM%"

- path: test_perf_sweep_ts.bat
  content: |
      @echo off
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      rem -ts / device-order sweep for the 27B model, 20k context only.
      rem
      rem   phase 1: MTP draft on Vulkan0, both device orders, Vulkan1 share 100..85
      rem   phase 2: MTP draft on Vulkan1 (frees Vulkan0 VRAM), Vulkan1 share 100/90/85
      rem   phase 3: no MTP at all, Vulkan0 share 15/25/30/35 (no draft VRAM cost)
      rem
      rem b = ub in {1536, 2048} (phase 1), 2048 only for phases 2-3
      rem -ot ".*=CPU" is kept everywhere (host buft of the first -dev device)
      rem
      rem logs: prompts_perf\sweep_ts\<tag>_b<B>.log
      rem summary CSV: prompts_perf\sweep_ts\summary.txt
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      setlocal enabledelayedexpansion
      taskkill /F /IM llama-server.exe /T >nul 2>&1
      ping -n 9 127.0.0.1 >nul
      
      set BIN=D:\shared\project\llama.cpp\build\bin
      set M=D:\shared\ai-models\Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf
      set PDIR=D:\shared\project\llama.cpp\prompts_perf
      set OUT=%PDIR%\sweep_ts
      if not exist "%OUT%" mkdir "%OUT%"
      set SUM=%OUT%\summary.txt
      echo tag,dev_order,ts,spec_dev,b,ub,prompt_tps,gen_tps > "%SUM%"
      
      set C=20000
      
      rem base: same as optimal.bat / test_perf_sweep_mtp.bat, -dev and -ts added per run
      set COMMON=-m %M% -ngl 99 -ot ".*=CPU" --load-mode none --pp-dev Vulkan0 ^
       -fa on -ctk q4_1 -ctv q4_1 -t 6 -tb 6 -n 4 --temp 0 -st -lv 5
      
      set SPEC0=--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-type-k q4_1 --spec-draft-type-v q4_1 --spec-draft-n-max 3 --spec-draft-device Vulkan0
      set SPEC1=--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-type-k q4_1 --spec-draft-type-v q4_1 --spec-draft-n-max 3 --spec-draft-device Vulkan1
      
      echo === phase 1: MTP on Vulkan0, device order A = Vulkan1 first, B = Vulkan0 first ===
      for %%B in (1536 2048) do (
          for %%F in (0 5 10 15) do (
              set /a R=100-%%F
              call :run A!R! "Vulkan1,Vulkan0" "!R!,%%F" Vulkan0 %%B "%SPEC0%"
          )
      )
      for %%B in (1536 2048) do (
          for %%F in (0 5 10 15) do (
              set /a R=100-%%F
              call :run B!R! "Vulkan0,Vulkan1" "%%F,!R!" Vulkan0 %%B "%SPEC0%"
          )
      )
      
      echo === phase 2: MTP on Vulkan1 ===
      for %%F in (0 10 15) do (
          set /a R=100-%%F
          call :run S1_!R! "Vulkan1,Vulkan0" "!R!,%%F" Vulkan1 2048 "%SPEC1%"
      )
      
      echo === phase 3: no MTP, more weights on Vulkan0 ===
      for %%F in (15 25 30 35) do (
          set /a R=100-%%F
          call :run NM_!R! "Vulkan1,Vulkan0" "!R!,%%F" none 2048 ""
      )
      
      echo.
      echo === sweep done, summary:
      type "%SUM%"
      goto :eof
      
      :run
      set TAG=%~1
      set DEV=%~2
      set TS=%~3
      set SPECDEV=%~4
      set B=%~5
      set SPEC=%~6
      set LOG=%OUT%\%TAG%_b%B%.log
      echo ============================================================
      echo %TAG% dev=%DEV% ts=%TS% spec_dev=%SPECDEV% b=%B% ub=%B% c=%C%
      taskkill /F /IM llama-server.exe /T >nul 2>&1
      ping -n 6 127.0.0.1 >nul
      "%BIN%\llama-cli.exe" %COMMON% -dev "%DEV%" -ts "%TS%" %SPEC% -c %C% -b %B% -ub %B% -f "%PDIR%\prompt_%C%.txt" > "%LOG%" 2>&1
      echo exit=%ERRORLEVEL%
      findstr /C:"Prompt: " "%LOG%"
      set V0=
      for /f "delims=" %%l in ('findstr /C:"Vulkan0 (RTX" "%LOG%"') do set V0=%%l
      echo !V0!
      for /f "tokens=3,7" %%a in ('findstr /C:"Prompt: " "%LOG%"') do (
          echo %TAG%,%DEV%,%TS%,%SPECDEV%,%B%,%B%,%%a,%%b >> "%SUM%"
          echo %TAG%,%TS%,%%a,%%b
      )
      findstr /C:"offloaded" "%LOG%"
      goto :eof
      
  referencedBy: {}

Fixed `test_perf_sweep_ts.bat`. Every run had been dying instantly with `error: invalid argument: 1536/2048`.

**Root cause**

In `call :run`, cmd treats commas as argument separators. The tensor-split value `!R!,%%F` (e.g. `100,0`) was therefore split into two arguments, shifting everything after it by one:

```
:run got  %3=100  %4=0  %5=Vulkan0  %6=1536   <- %6 was meant to be the spec flags
```

So the command line became `-ts 100 1536 -c 20000 ...` (`-ts` swallowed only `100`), and `1536` was left as a positional argument -> `invalid argument`. That's why all 9 logs in `prompts_perf/sweep_ts/` are 31 bytes and named `..._bVulkan0.log` (`%B%` had picked up `Vulkan0`).

**Changes**

- Quoted the tensor-split at all 4 call sites: `"!R!,%%F"` / `"%%F,!R!"`. Verified with a throwaway cmd test that this keeps the value as one argument and still passes an empty spec correctly for phase 3.
- Quoted `-dev "%DEV%"` and `-ts "%TS%"` in the `llama-cli` invocation for the same reason (both contain commas).
- CSV rows were also broken: `%DEV%` (`Vulkan1,Vulkan0`) and `%TS%` (`100,0`) each added an extra field, so rows had 10 columns against an 8-column header. Added `DEVQ`/`TSQ` (`%DEV:,=+%`, `%TS:,=+%`) and write those; rows are now 8 fields, e.g. `A100,Vulkan1+Vulkan0,100+0,Vulkan0,1536,1536,122.0,3.4`.
- The diagnostic `findstr /C:"Vulkan0 (RTX"` never matched this build's logs (they print `Vulkan0 (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU)`), so it echoed `ECHO is off.`. Now it uses `"Vulkan0 ("`.

**Verification**

I ran a dry-run copy (no model, no taskkill, fake llama-cli output) using the real loop and `:run` logic: 23 runs, correct tags/`-dev`/`-ts`/spec per run, `-b`/`-ub` correct, tps parsed from `[ Prompt: ... | Generation: ... ]`, and a clean 23-row CSV. Temp files removed.

Note: the 9 stale `*_bVulkan0.log` files from the failed run are still in `prompts_perf/sweep_ts/` (they won't be overwritten, since names are now `_b1536`/`_b2048`). Say the word and I'll delete them.

      struct llama_model_params common_model_params_to_llama(common_params & params) {
          auto mparams = llama_model_default_params();
      
          // scheduling only: the device list order decides where the weights are placed, the prefill
          // device is just appended to make sure it is available to the scheduler
          if (params.pp_dev != nullptr) {
              auto it = std::find(params.devices.begin(), params.devices.end(), params.pp_dev);
      
              bool pp_appended = false;
              if (it == params.devices.end()) {
                  auto back = params.devices.end();
                  if (!params.devices.empty() && params.devices.back() == nullptr) {
                      --back;
                  }
                  params.devices.insert(back, params.pp_dev);
                  pp_appended = true;
              }
      
              // the prefill device only receives weight copies, it should not store any layers. with
              // the default split (by free memory) it would claim the last layers, which moves their
              // KV cache and decode norm ops onto it and splits every decode graph. give it a zero
              // layer share unless the user set one explicitly
              bool ts_set = false;
              for (size_t i = 0; i < llama_max_devices(); ++i) {
                  if (params.tensor_split[i] != 0.0f) {
                      ts_set = true;
                      break;
                  }
              }
              size_t n_devs = 0;
              for (auto * dev : params.devices) {
                  if (dev == nullptr) {
                      break;
                  }
                  n_devs++;
              }
              if (pp_appended && !ts_set && n_devs >= 2) {
                  const size_t pp_idx = std::find(params.devices.begin(), params.devices.begin() + n_devs, params.pp_dev) - params.devices.begin();
                  for (size_t i = 0; i < llama_max_devices(); ++i) {
                      params.tensor_split[i] = i == pp_idx ? 0.0f : 1.0f;
                  }
                  COM_INF("%s", "pp_device layer share = 0 (weights are copied to it per batch, layers stay on the other devices)\n");
              }
      
              COM_INF("pp_device = %s (%s)\n", ggml_backend_dev_name(params.pp_dev), ggml_backend_dev_description(params.pp_dev));
      
              if (params.n_gpu_layers != 0) {
                  COM_WRN("%s", "--pp-dev copies the weights of offloaded layers to the prefill device on every prefill batch\n");
              }
          }
      
          if (!params.devices.empty()) {
              mparams.devices = params.devices.data();
          }
      
          mparams.n_gpu_layers    = params.n_gpu_layers;
          mparams.main_gpu        = params.main_gpu;
          mparams.split_mode      = params.split_mode;
          mparams.load_mode       = params.load_mode;
          mparams.lazy_mode = params.lazy_mode;
          mparams.tensor_split    = params.tensor_split;
          mparams.check_tensors   = params.check_tensors;
          mparams.use_extra_bufts = !params.no_extra_bufts;
          mparams.no_host         = params.no_host;
      
          if (params.kv_overrides.empty()) {
              mparams.kv_overrides = NULL;
          } else {
              GGML_ASSERT(params.kv_overrides.back().key[0] == 0 && "KV overrides not terminated with empty key");
              mparams.kv_overrides = params.kv_overrides.data();
          }
      
          if (params.tensor_buft_overrides.empty()) {
              mparams.tensor_buft_overrides = NULL;
          } else {
              GGML_ASSERT(params.tensor_buft_overrides.back().pattern == nullptr && "Tensor buffer overrides not terminated with empty pattern");
              mparams.tensor_buft_overrides = params.tensor_buft_overrides.data();
          }
      
          mparams.progress_callback           = params.load_progress_callback;
          mparams.progress_callback_user_data = params.load_progress_callback_user_data;
          mparams.no_alloc                    = params.no_alloc;
          mparams.load_mtp                    = std::find(params.speculative.types.begin(), params.speculative.types.end(), COMMON_SPECULATIVE_TYPE_DRAFT_MTP) != params.speculative.types.end();
      
          return mparams;
      }

      // Helper function to parse tensor buffer override strings
      static void parse_tensor_buffer_overrides(const std::string & value, std::vector<llama_model_tensor_buft_override> & overrides) {
          ggml_backend_load_all();
      
          std::map<std::string, ggml_backend_buffer_type_t> buft_list;
          for (size_t i = 0; i < ggml_backend_dev_count(); ++i) {
              auto * dev = ggml_backend_dev_get(i);
              auto * buft = ggml_backend_dev_buffer_type(dev);
              if (buft) {
                  buft_list[ggml_backend_buft_name(buft)] = buft;
              }
          }
      
          for (const auto & override : string_split<std::string>(value, ',')) {
              std::string::size_type pos = override.find('=');
              if (pos == std::string::npos) {
                  throw std::invalid_argument("invalid value");
              }
              std::string tensor_name = override.substr(0, pos);
              std::string buffer_type = override.substr(pos + 1);
      
              if (buft_list.find(buffer_type) == buft_list.end()) {
                  printf("Available buffer types:\n");
                  for (const auto & it : buft_list) {
                      printf("  %s\n", ggml_backend_buft_name(it.second));
                  }
                  throw std::invalid_argument("unknown buffer type");
              }
              // keep strings alive and avoid leaking memory by storing them in a static vector
              static std::list<std::string> buft_overrides;
              buft_overrides.push_back(tensor_name);
              overrides.push_back({buft_overrides.back().c_str(), buft_list.at(buffer_type)});
          }
      }

      static std::vector<ggml_backend_dev_t> parse_device_list(const std::string & value) {
          std::vector<ggml_backend_dev_t> devices;
          auto dev_names = string_split<std::string>(value, ',');
          if (dev_names.empty()) {
              throw std::invalid_argument("no devices specified");
          }
          if (dev_names.size() == 1 && dev_names[0] == "none") {
              devices.push_back(nullptr);
          } else {
              ggml_backend_load_all();
              for (const auto & device : dev_names) {
                  auto * dev = ggml_backend_dev_by_name(device.c_str());
                  if (!dev || ggml_backend_dev_type(dev) == GGML_BACKEND_DEVICE_TYPE_CPU) {
                      throw std::invalid_argument(string_format("invalid device: %s", device.c_str()));
                  }
                  devices.push_back(dev);
              }
              devices.push_back(nullptr);
          }
          return devices;
      }

> _Reasoning_
> Key insight: `parse_tensor_buffer_overrides` builds `buft_list` from **device default buffer types only**: `ggml_backend_dev_buffer_type(dev)` for each registered backend device. So valid names are the device buft names: "CPU", "Vulkan0", "Vulkan1", "CUDA0", etc. The host buffer type (`ggml_backend_dev_host_buffer_type(dev)`) is NOT included here... unless `ggml_backend_dev_buffer_type` for Vulkan returns the device buft named "Vulkan0".
> 
> So `-ot ".*=CPU"` sets all tensors to the CPU buffer type (the plain system CPU). The comment in the sweep scripts says "host buft of the first -dev device" — that's probably inaccurate; it's actually the CPU buft.
> 
> Hmm. But the user's feature: "-ot \".*=CPU\" + --load-mode none -> weights in Vulkan1_Host (zero-copy decode)". Let's understand: When a tensor is assigned the CPU buft, and the scheduler/extra bufts... Actually llama.cpp has "extra bufts" (use_extra_bufts) which allow host buffer types of devices to be used. Also `--load-mode none`?
> 
> The important part for the user's question: they want -ot to place *some weights* on Vulkan0 (device VRAM) while the rest stay in the host/CPU buffer, with `-dev Vulkan0,Vulkan1` and `--pp-dev Vulkan0`.
> 
> So basically `-ot` supports multiple comma-separated overrides; pattern matching picks the first match? Let's check llama-model-loader.cpp:1228 to see how patterns are applied and whether later overrides override earlier ones ("last match wins" or "first match wins").
>

      // CPU: ACCEL -> GPU host -> CPU extra -> CPU
      static buft_list_t make_cpu_buft_list(const std::vector<llama_device> & devices, bool use_extra_bufts, bool no_host) {
          buft_list_t buft_list;
      
          // add ACCEL buffer types
          for (size_t i = 0; i < ggml_backend_dev_count(); ++i) {
              ggml_backend_dev_t dev = ggml_backend_dev_get(i);
              if (ggml_backend_dev_type(dev) == GGML_BACKEND_DEVICE_TYPE_ACCEL) {
                  auto * buft = ggml_backend_dev_buffer_type(dev);
                  // skip
                  if (buft != ggml_backend_cpu_buffer_type()) {
                      buft_list.emplace_back(dev, buft);
                  }
              }
          }
      
          // add a host buffer type
          // storing the tensors in a host buffer is useful when the processing of large batches
          // is offloaded to a GPU device, since it reduces the time spent on data transfers
          // generally, this will be done using the first device in the list
          // a better approach would be to handle this on a weight-by-weight basis using the offload_op
          // function of the device to determine if it would benefit from being stored in a host buffer
          if (!no_host) {
              for (const auto & dev : devices) {
                  ggml_backend_buffer_type_t buft = ggml_backend_dev_host_buffer_type(dev.dev);
                  if (buft) {
                      buft_list.emplace_back(dev.dev, buft);
                      break;
                  }
              }
          }
      
          // add extra buffer types
          if (use_extra_bufts) {
              auto * cpu_dev = ggml_backend_dev_by_type(GGML_BACKEND_DEVICE_TYPE_CPU);
              if (cpu_dev == nullptr) {
                  throw std::runtime_error(format("%s: no CPU backend found", __func__));
              }
      
              auto * cpu_reg = ggml_backend_dev_backend_reg(cpu_dev);
              auto ggml_backend_dev_get_extra_bufts_fn = (ggml_backend_dev_get_extra_bufts_t)
                  ggml_backend_reg_get_proc_address(cpu_reg, "ggml_backend_dev_get_extra_bufts");
              if (ggml_backend_dev_get_extra_bufts_fn) {
                  ggml_backend_buffer_type_t * extra_bufts = ggml_backend_dev_get_extra_bufts_fn(cpu_dev);
                  while (extra_bufts && *extra_bufts) {
                      buft_list.emplace_back(cpu_dev, *extra_bufts);
                      ++extra_bufts;
                  }
              }
          }
      
          // add the CPU buffer type
          for (size_t i = 0; i < ggml_backend_dev_count(); ++i) {
              ggml_backend_dev_t dev = ggml_backend_dev_get(i);
              if (ggml_backend_dev_type(dev) == GGML_BACKEND_DEVICE_TYPE_CPU) {
                  buft_list.emplace_back(dev, ggml_backend_dev_buffer_type(dev));
              }
          }
      
          return buft_list;
      }
      
      // GPU: split if LLAMA_SPLIT_MODE_ROW -> GPU
      static buft_list_t make_gpu_buft_list(ggml_backend_dev_t dev, llama_split_mode split_mode, const float * tensor_split) {
          buft_list_t buft_list;
      
          // add the device split buffer type if requested and available
          if (split_mode == LLAMA_SPLIT_MODE_ROW) {
              ggml_backend_reg_t reg = ggml_backend_dev_backend_reg(dev);
              auto ggml_backend_split_buffer_type_fn = (ggml_backend_split_buffer_type_t)
                  ggml_backend_reg_get_proc_address(reg, "ggml_backend_split_buffer_type");
              if (ggml_backend_split_buffer_type_fn) {
                  size_t dev_index = [&]() {
                      auto * reg = ggml_backend_dev_backend_reg(dev);
                      for (size_t i = 0; i < ggml_backend_reg_dev_count(reg); ++i) {
                          if (ggml_backend_reg_dev_get(reg, i) == dev) {
                              return i;
                          }
                      }
                      throw std::runtime_error(format("device %s not found in its backend reg", ggml_backend_dev_name(dev)));
                  }();
                  auto * buft = ggml_backend_split_buffer_type_fn(dev_index, tensor_split);
                  if (buft != nullptr) {
                      buft_list.emplace_back(dev, buft);
                  }
              } else {
                  throw std::runtime_error(format("device %s does not support split buffers", ggml_backend_dev_name(dev)));
              }
          }
      
          // add the device default buffer type
          buft_list.emplace_back(dev, ggml_backend_dev_buffer_type(dev));
      
          // add the device extra buffer type (if any)
          ggml_backend_reg_t reg = ggml_backend_dev_backend_reg(dev);

      Findings:
      
      1. `-ot ".*=CPU"` does not mean plain CPU buffers: `select_weight_buft` picks `Vulkan_Host`, so weights land
         in pinned host memory and the copy to V0 becomes a single-stage DMA (~6 GB/s).
      2. `--load-mode none` is required with CPU overrides (mmap page-cache re-reads cost ~7%; the loader warns
         about it).
      3. **Weight residency on Vulkan0 is not needed.** D8 with zero residency matches D4 at ub1536 and then keeps
         scaling to ub2048 because the freed VRAM absorbs the larger compute buffer (581 MiB at ub2048, 849 MiB at
         ub3072).
      4. ubatch size is the dominant lever: weights are streamed once per ubatch, so doubling ub nearly halves the
         copy volume per token. It collapses only when the V0 footprint passes ~4.5 GB (weights + compute buffer +
         desktop), where compute slows 3-10x.
      5. `GGML_SCHED_COPY_LOOKAHEAD` is net negative on this hardware and should be removed before committing
         (see 8.10).
      6. `GGML_SCHED_PROFILE` writes to `stderr` via `fprintf`, so `--log-file` does not capture it. Redirect
         `2>>` in the bat.
      
      ### 8.10 Lookahead double-buffering PoC (negative, remove before commit)
      
      `GGML_SCHED_COPY_LOOKAHEAD` deferred freeing of copy tensors via `alloc_deps` and prefetched weight copies
      `L` splits ahead. Correct (identical output at every L) but never faster:
      
      - RTX 4050 reports `single_queue = true` (`ggml-vulkan.cpp:6880`: same queue family and `queueCount == 1`),
        so `transfer_queue` is aliased to `compute_queue` and `async_use_transfer_queue = false`. Copy and compute
        share one FIFO, so GPU-side overlap is impossible on Vulkan0.
      - L=8 neutral, L=24/64 actively worse; with any V0 residency it spills VRAM (D4 l8: 49.3 t/s).
      
      Verdict: drop the lookahead code, keep the gate and the profiling helper.

> 4. CPU buft

              // add CPU buffer types as a fallback
              buft_list.insert(buft_list.end(), pimpl->cpu_buft_list.begin(), pimpl->cpu_buft_list.end());
              pimpl->gpu_buft_list.emplace(dev.dev, std::move(buft_list));

- path: test_perf_sweep_ts.bat
  content: |
      @echo off
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      rem -ts / device-order sweep for the 27B model, 20k context only.
      rem
      rem   phase 1: MTP draft on Vulkan0, both device orders, Vulkan1 share 100..85
      rem   phase 2: MTP draft on Vulkan1 (frees Vulkan0 VRAM), Vulkan1 share 100/90/85
      rem   phase 3: no MTP at all, Vulkan0 share 15/25/30/35 (no draft VRAM cost)
      rem   phase 4: Vulkan0 first, a few layers stay resident in Vulkan0 VRAM
      rem
      rem b = ub in {1536, 2048} (phase 1), 2048 only for phases 2-4
      rem
      rem -ot is passed per run (7th arg). patterns are matched in order and the first match wins,
      rem so a layer specific pattern must come before the catch-all ".*=CPU".
      rem "=CPU" never puts weights in a device VRAM: the loader reroutes it through
      rem select_weight_buft() to the CPU buft list, whose only device entry is the host buft of the
      rem FIRST -dev device (Vulkan0 -> global pinned Vulkan_Host, Vulkan1 -> Vulkan1_Host).
      rem to place weights on the RTX 4050 name its device buft: "<pattern>=Vulkan0".
      rem only CPU, Vulkan0 and Vulkan1 are accepted names (host bufts are not listed by -ot).
      rem
      rem logs: prompts_perf\sweep_ts\<tag>_b<B>.log
      rem summary CSV: prompts_perf\sweep_ts\summary.txt
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      setlocal enabledelayedexpansion
      taskkill /F /IM llama-server.exe /T >nul 2>&1
      ping -n 9 127.0.0.1 >nul
      
      set BIN=D:\shared\project\llama.cpp\build\bin
      set M=D:\shared\ai-models\Qwen3.8-27B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf
      set PDIR=D:\shared\project\llama.cpp\prompts_perf
      set OUT=%PDIR%\sweep_ts
      if not exist "%OUT%" mkdir "%OUT%"
      set SUM=%OUT%\summary.txt
      echo tag,dev_order,ts,spec_dev,b,ub,prompt_tps,gen_tps > "%SUM%"
      
      set C=20000rem base: same as optimal.bat / test_perf_sweep_mtp.bat, -dev/-ts/-ot added per run
      set COMMON=-m %M% -ngl 99 --load-mode none --pp-dev Vulkan0 ^
       -fa on -ctk q4_1 -ctv q4_1 -t 6 -tb 6 -n 4 --temp 0 -st -lv 5
      
      rem the 27B is 64 layers, ~261 MiB per layer; Vulkan0 has 5078 MiB free and needs
      rem ~600-750 MiB of compute buffer plus the MTP draft, so 8-12 layers fit
      rem use the quoted set form: the layer patterns contain regex "|" and "()"
      set "OT0=.*=CPU"
      set "OT8=blk\.[0-7]\.=Vulkan0,%OT0%"
      set "OT12=blk\.([0-9]|1[01])\.=Vulkan0,%OT0%"
      
      set SPEC0=--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-type-k q4_1 --spec-draft-type-v q4_1 --spec-draft-n-max 3 --spec-draft-device Vulkan0
      set SPEC1=--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-type-k q4_1 --spec-draft-type-v q4_1 --spec-draft-n-max 3 --spec-draft-device Vulkan1
      
      echo === phase 1: MTP on Vulkan0, device order A = Vulkan1 first, B = Vulkan0 first ===
      for %%B in (1536 2048) do (
          for %%F in (0 5 10 15) do (
              set /a R=100-%%F
              call :run A!R! "Vulkan1,Vulkan0" "!R!,%%F" Vulkan0 %%B "%SPEC0%" "%OT0%"
          )
      )
      for %%B in (1536 2048) do (
          for %%F in (0 5 10 15) do (
              set /a R=100-%%F
              call :run B!R! "Vulkan0,Vulkan1" "%%F,!R!" Vulkan0 %%B "%SPEC0%" "%OT0%"
          )
      )
      
      echo === phase 2: MTP on Vulkan1 ===
      for %%F in (0 10 15) do (
          set /a R=100-%%F
          call :run S1_!R! "Vulkan1,Vulkan0" "!R!,%%F" Vulkan1 2048 "%SPEC1%" "%OT0%"
      )
      
      echo === phase 3: no MTP, more weights on Vulkan0 ===
      for %%F in (15 25 30 35) do (
          set /a R=100-%%F
          call :run NM_!R! "Vulkan1,Vulkan0" "!R!,%%F" none 2048 "" "%OT0%"
      )
      
      echo === phase 4: 8/12 layers resident in Vulkan0 VRAM (Vulkan0 first, share matched) ===
      rem -ts is in -dev order, layers are assigned to devices in contiguous ranges
      rem (llama-model.cpp load_tensors, upper_bound on the normalized split points), so the
      rem resident layer range must match Vulkan0's layer share
      rem R0 is the control: same layer share, no resident weights
      call :run R0  "Vulkan0,Vulkan1" "12.5,87.5"   Vulkan0 2048 "%SPEC0%" "%OT0%"
      call :run R8  "Vulkan0,Vulkan1" "12.5,87.5"   Vulkan0 2048 "%SPEC0%" "%OT8%"
      call :run R12 "Vulkan0,Vulkan1" "18.75,81.25" Vulkan0 2048 "%SPEC0%" "%OT12%"
      
      echo.
      echo === sweep done, summary:
      type "%SUM%"
      goto :eof
      
      :run
      set TAG=%~1
      set DEV=%~2
      set TS=%~3
      set SPECDEV=%~4
      set B=%~5
      set SPEC=%~6
      set OT=%~7
      rem CSV fields cannot contain commas, so device order and tensor split use + as separator
      set DEVQ=%DEV:,=+%
      set TSQ=%TS:,=+%
      set LOG=%OUT%\%TAG%_b%B%.log
      echo ============================================================
      echo %TAG% dev=%DEV% ts=%TS% spec_dev=%SPECDEV% b=%B% ub=%B% c=%C% ot=%OT%
      taskkill /F /IM llama-server.exe /T >nul 2>&1
      ping -n 6 127.0.0.1 >nul
      "%BIN%\llama-cli.exe" %COMMON% -dev "%DEV%" -ts "%TS%" -ot "%OT%" %SPEC% -c %C% -b %B% -ub %B% -f "%PDIR%\prompt_%C%.txt" > "%LOG%" 2>&1
      echo exit=%ERRORLEVEL%
      findstr /C:"Prompt: " "%LOG%"
      set V0=
      for /f "delims=" %%l in ('findstr /C:"Vulkan0 (" "%LOG%"') do set V0=%%l
      echo !V0!
      for /f "tokens=3,7" %%a in ('findstr /C:"Prompt: " "%LOG%"') do (
          echo %TAG%,%DEVQ%,%TSQ%,%SPECDEV%,%B%,%B%,%%a,%%b >> "%SUM%"
          echo %TAG%,%TS%,%%a,%%b
      )
      findstr /C:"offloaded" "%LOG%"
      goto :eof
      
  referencedBy: {}

> _Reasoning_
> The dry run caught a real bug: the R12 call fails with `'1[01])\.' is not recognized as an internal or external command`. This is the `call` + `|` issue: inside the quoted arg, `|` in a `call`ed command line gets interpreted because `call` re-parses the line and the `|` breaks out. Known cmd behavior: `call :label "a|b"` → the pipe is still processed? Apparently yes, cmd's call parsing splits on `|` even inside quotes in some cases. Actually the error message shows cmd treated `1[01])\.=...` as a command, so the `|` acted as a pipe despite quotes.
> 
> Hmm. The first part `blk\.([0-9]` — the `(`? no, the pipe split.
> 
> Fix options:
> 1. Avoid `|` in the regex: use separate comma-separated patterns instead of alternation. E.g. for 12 layers: `blk\.[0-9]\.=Vulkan0,blk\.1[01]\.=Vulkan0,.*=CPU` (two patterns, no pipe). 
> 2. Or avoid `call` for phase 4 by inlining.
> 3. Or escape `|` as `^|` when passing — messy with quoting.
> 
> Option 1 is simplest and keeps the same semantics: patterns are checked in order; both specific patterns come before the catch-all.
> 
> So: `set "OT12=blk\.[0-9]\.=Vulkan0,blk\.1[01]\.=Vulkan0,%OT0%"`.
> 
> That covers layers 0-9 and 10-11 = 0..11. Good, no `|` or `()` in the value.
> 
> Let me also double check `[0-9]` brackets are fine in cmd (yes) and `\.` fine.
> 
> But wait — is `(` also a problem? Earlier the error was specifically about the pipe. With option 1, there are no parens either. 
> 
> Now also should I reconsider the OT8 pattern: `blk\.[0-7]\.=Vulkan0,.*=CPU` worked fine in the dry run (echoed correctly). Keep.
> 
> Apply the fix and re-run the dry run.

Stale logs cleared and the build/behaviour verified. Here is what I found and what I changed.

## 1. Stale logs
Deleted the 9 failed-run files `prompts_perf/sweep_ts/*_bVulkan0.log` (all 31 bytes of `error: invalid argument: ...`). `summary.txt` now holds just the header again.

## 2. How `-ot ".*=CPU"` actually resolves

- **Which names are legal**: only `CPU`, `Vulkan0`, `Vulkan1`. `parse_tensor_buffer_overrides` (`common/arg.cpp:252`) enumerates `ggml_backend_dev_buffer_type(dev)` only, never `ggml_backend_dev_host_buffer_type(dev)`, so `Vulkan_Host` / `Vulkan1_Host` are **not** addressable from `-ot`. Verified by running `llama-cli.exe -ot "x=y"`, which prints the list: `CPU`, `Vulkan0`, `Vulkan1`.
- **`=CPU` is not the CPU buffer**: `src/llama-model-loader.cpp:1232` reroutes a matched CPU override through `select_weight_buft(..., buft_list_cpu)`. That list comes from `make_cpu_buft_list` (`src/llama-model.cpp:1031`) and its only device entry is **the host buft of the first `-dev` device that has one** (the loop `break`s after the first hit). So `.*=CPU` can never reach any device VRAM, no matter the `-ts`; it only picks *which host buft*:
  - `-dev Vulkan0,Vulkan1` -> Vulkan0 first -> discrete 4050 -> global pinned `Vulkan_Host`, bound to vk device 0 (DMA staging, not in-place readable).
  - `-dev Vulkan1,Vulkan0` -> `Vulkan1_Host`, the 760M UMA aperture (zero-copy for the iGPU).
  - Evidence from your own mtp sweep log (`-dev Vulkan1`): `tensor token_embd.weight (682 MiB q4_K) buffer type overridden to Vulkan1_Host`.
- **First match wins** (`break`, `src/llama-model-loader.cpp:1247`), so a layer-specific pattern must be listed **before** the catch-all.

## 3. Recipe to put weights on Vulkan0

```
-ot "blk\.[0-7]\.=Vulkan0,.*=CPU"
```

Resident layers land in the 4050's device buft: no per-prefill-batch copy for them, and decode reads them in place (host-buft weights on a discrete card cannot be).

Sizing from your own logs: 64 layers, 16735 MiB weights (~261 MiB/layer), Vulkan0 5078 MiB free, compute buffer 582 MiB at ub 2048 (up to ~730 with MTP). So 8 layers ~2.1 GB, 12 layers ~3.1 GB; 16 would spill.

Align `-ts` with the resident range: layers are assigned contiguously in `-dev` order (`upper_bound` on normalized split points, `src/llama-model.cpp:1480-1490`), so 8/64 -> `-ts 12.5,87.5`, 12/64 -> `-ts 18.75,81.25`. Otherwise the layer's KV/norms land on the other device while its weights sit on Vulkan0.

## 4. Changes in `test_perf_sweep_ts.bat`

- `-ot` moved out of `COMMON` and is now the 7th argument of `:run` (order matters, so it has to be one string).
- `OT0=.*=CPU`, `OT8=blk\.[0-7]\.=Vulkan0,.*=CPU`, `OT12=blk\.[0-9]\.=Vulkan0,blk\.1[01]\.=Vulkan0,.*=CPU`.
- New **phase 4** (`-dev Vulkan0,Vulkan1`, MTP on Vulkan0, ub 2048): `R0` = control with the same layer share and no residency, `R8`, `R12`.
- Header comments document the resolution rules; `:run` echoes `ot=` per run.

Two cmd traps found by dry-running, both fixed: `call :run` splits unquoted commas (hence quotes around `-ts`), and a `|` inside a quoted `call` argument is still parsed as a pipe, which is why `OT12` uses two plain patterns instead of `([0-9]|1[01])`.

**Verification**: dry run of the real loop/`:run` logic (no model) -> 26 runs, correct `-dev/-ts/-ot/spec` per run, 8-field CSV rows for all of `A/B/S1/NM/R0/R8/R12`, 0 cmd errors. Both override strings accepted by real arg parsing (`llama-cli -ot "<spec>" -h`, exit 0, no `unknown buffer type`).

One thing to be aware of for phase 4: because order is `Vulkan0,Vulkan1`, all non-resident weights sit in the pinned `Vulkan_Host` (4050-owned staging), not `Vulkan1_Host`. If you want the UMA zero-copy base plus partial residency, use `-dev Vulkan1,Vulkan0` and give Vulkan0 the *last* layers (`-ts 87.5,12.5` + `blk\.(5[6-9]|6[0-3])\.`) - note that pattern needs no `|` workaround only if written as two plain ranges.

Your answers pin the design down. Let me confirm the shape of it before editing:

**Design** (reuses the existing `-ot` / `tensor_buft_overrides` mechanism, no hand-written patterns):
- You pass `-dev Vulkan0,Vulkan1 -ts 15,85 --pp-dev Vulkan0 --pp-dev-resident`.
- In `llama_model::load_tensors`, after the layer split is computed, the model knows exactly which layers went to Vulkan0 (with `-ts 15,85` that is 10 of 64). It rewrites the override list it hands the loader as `<blk.N. >=Vulkan0 for each of those layers>, <your -ot patterns>`, so those layers' weights land in the 4050's VRAM and everything else keeps following `.*=CPU`.
- Residency follows `-ts` automatically, and it cannot disagree with the split, which is what caused the hand-written `blk\.[0-7]\.` + `-ts 12.5,87.5` coupling.

> _Reasoning_
> Now answer the user's question with evidence, and mention the output-layer caveat + the host-buft/order interaction + recommendation for phase 4 config.
> 
> Summary of the answer:
> 
> **Yes, device order independent.** Because residency is decided from `dev_layer[]` (the layer split), not from the index you position the device at.
> 
> Evidence (gemma-4-E4B, 42 layers, 3220 MiB weights):
> | config | resident | Vulkan0 buft | non-resident buft |
> | `-dev Vulkan0,Vulkan1 -ts 15,85` | 7 layers | 361.22 MiB | Vulkan_Host 2859.08 |
> | `-dev Vulkan1,Vulkan0 -ts 85,15` | 5 layers | 251.58 MiB | Vulkan1_Host 2968.72 |
> | no -ts (split by free mem) | 3 layers | 153.20 MiB | Vulkan1_Host 3067.10 |
> control `-dev Vulkan0,Vulkan1 -ts 15,85` without the flag: Vulkan0 0 MiB, Vulkan_Host 3220.30 MiB.
> 
> Sums match exactly (3220.30), so nothing is duplicated or dropped.
> 
> Note the count differences are geometry, not order-dependence: with 43 "layer slots" (42 + output) and -ts 15/85, Vulkan0's first-device share is slots 0..6 (7), while as the *second* device with 85/15 it takes slots 37..41 (5 repeating layers, plus dev_output). The rule is the same either way: whatever the split gave it.
> 
> **Caveats:**
> 
> 1. `--pp-dev` not in `-dev` → appended with 0 layer share → no layers → warning `no layer is assigned to device Vulkan0, no weights kept resident`. Verified. So list the pp device in `-dev` (as you do).
> 
> 2. Order still decides where the *non-resident* weights live: the host buft is the first `-dev` device's (`-dev Vulkan0,Vulkan1` → pinned `Vulkan_Host` owned by the 4050; reverse → `Vulkan1_Host`, UMA, in-place readable). So `-ts 85,15` with Vulkan0 first is the bad combination (85% of layers on the 760M but their weights in a 4050-owned pinned buffer → copies per op). For the residency experiment the better geometry is `-dev Vulkan1,Vulkan0 -ts 85,15`: the 760M reads its weights in place from Vulkan1_Host, and Vulkan0 keeps its own 5-10 layers resident. Phase 4 currently uses `-dev Vulkan0,Vulkan1 -ts 15,85` (your stated config) — say the word and I'll switch/add it.
> 
> 3. Known gap: only `blk\.N\.` tensors get residency. When Vulkan0 owns `dev_output` (which happens when it is the *last* device in -dev), `output.weight` (994 MiB on the 27B) stays in the host buft and is copied per batch/token. Worth extending to `output\.` = pp dev buft when `dev_output.dev == pp_dev`. Offer.
> 
> Also mention verification caveat: the perf numbers from gemma are not meaningful (tiny prompt); only functional.
> 
> And mention what changed in code (files) briefly and that build/verify is done. Keep it concise. Also note the earlier build tooling discovery (build_pp.bat) maybe not needed.
> 
> Let me write the final answer with a compact table and the offer. Also suggest followups.

Yes — order-independent, because residency is decided from `dev_layer[]` (the layer split), not from the device's position in the list. Verified on gemma-4-E4B (42 layers, 3220.30 MiB weights, same flags as the sweep):

| config | `keeping the weights of` | Vulkan0 buft | rest |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-dev Vulkan0,Vulkan1 -ts 15,85` (control, no flag) | - | 0.00 MiB | Vulkan_Host 3220.30 MiB |
| `-dev Vulkan0,Vulkan1 -ts 15,85` | 7 layers | 361.22 MiB | Vulkan_Host 2859.08 MiB |
| `-dev Vulkan1,Vulkan0 -ts 85,15` | 5 layers | 251.58 MiB | Vulkan1_Host 2968.72 MiB |
| `-dev Vulkan1,Vulkan0`, no `-ts` (split by free mem) | 3 layers | 153.20 MiB | Vulkan1_Host 3067.10 MiB |

Budgets add up exactly everywhere (361.22 + 2859.08 = 251.58 + 2968.72 = 3220.30), so no weight is dropped or duplicated. The differing counts are geometry, not order-dependence: with 43 slots (42 layers + output) `-ts 15,85` gives the first device slots 0-6, while as the second device `-ts 85,15` gives it slots 37-41. Either way it gets exactly what the split gave it.

**Three caveats**

1. `--pp-dev` not listed in `-dev` -> it is appended with a zero layer share, so there is nothing to keep resident. Verified: `W load_tensors: no layer is assigned to device Vulkan0, no weights kept resident` (also for `-ts 0,100`). Needs `-dev Vulkan0,Vulkan1 ... --pp-dev Vulkan0` as you have it.
2. Order still decides where the *non-resident* weights live, since that is the first `-dev` device's host buft: `-dev Vulkan0,Vulkan1` -> pinned `Vulkan_Host` owned by the 4050; reverse -> `Vulkan1_Host` (UMA, read in place). So `-ts 85,15` with Vulkan0 *first* is the bad pairing (85% of layers run on the 760M but their weights sit in a 4050-owned pinned buffer). For the residency experiment the better geometry is `-dev Vulkan1,Vulkan0 -ts 85,15`: the 760M reads its weights in place and the 4050 keeps its own layers resident. Phase 4 currently uses your stated `-dev Vulkan0,Vulkan1 -ts 15,85`.
3. Gap: only `blk\.N\.` tensors are covered. When Vulkan0 owns `dev_output` (i.e. it is the last device in `-dev`, which is the case in the reverse order), `output.weight` (994 MiB on the 27B) stays in the host buft and is copied per batch/token. Easy to extend to `output\.` when `dev_output.dev == pp_dev`.

Code changes (all built, `llama-cli.exe` links clean): `--pp-dev-resident` in `common/arg.cpp` + `common_params::pp_dev_resident`, lifted to `llama_model_params::pp_dev_resident` in `common/common.cpp`, and consumed in `llama_model::load_tensors` right after the layer split is computed, where it prepends `blk\.<il>\.=<pp dev buft>` overrides for exactly the pp device's layers ahead of your `-ot` list. `test_perf_sweep_ts.bat` now passes extra flags as an 8th `:run` arg; phase 4 is `R15`/`R25` (`-ts 15,85` / `25,75` + flag, ub 2048) and the hand-written `OT8`/`OT12` patterns are gone. Bat dry run: 25 runs, 8-field CSV, no cmd errors. The gemma timing numbers are not meaningful for perf (tiny prompt), only the placement was checked.

> Let me explain UMA briefly: Vulkan1 = AMD Radeon 760M iGPU, unified memory architecture — its "VRAM" is the same physical DRAM as system RAM. In this branch, UMA devices get a per-device host buffer type (`Vulkan1_Host`) which is a device-owned, host-visible buffer → weights placed there are read in place by the 760M with zero copies (that's the whole zero-copy decode win documented in handoff.md 8.7). Discrete Vulkan0 (RTX 4050) has no such thing: it gets the global pinned `Vulkan_Host` (allocated in system RAM, bound to vk device 0, DMA staging to the 4050). So "UMA variant" = putting Vulkan1 first in -dev so that the `.*=CPU` weights resolve to `Vulkan1_Host` (zero-copy for the 760M) while Vulkan0 keeps its own layers resident — vs the "pinned/staging" variant where Vulkan0 is first.

static bool ggml_backend_vk_device_supports_buft(ggml_backend_dev_t dev, ggml_backend_buffer_type_t buft) {
    if (buft->iface.get_name != ggml_backend_vk_buffer_type_name) {
        return false;
    }

    ggml_backend_vk_device_context * ctx = (ggml_backend_vk_device_context *)dev->context;
    ggml_backend_vk_buffer_type_context * buft_ctx = (ggml_backend_vk_buffer_type_context *)buft->context;

    return buft_ctx->device->idx == ctx->device;
}

`supports_buft` confirms the order effect: the per-device `Vulkan1_Host` has a real per-device context (`buft_ctx->device->idx == ctx->device`), while the global pinned `Vulkan_Host` is bound to vk device 0 and is pure staging. So order A = in-place reads for the 760M, order B = everything staged through pinned system RAM.

**What "UMA variant" meant:** Vulkan1 is the Radeon 760M, an integrated GPU whose "VRAM" is the same physical DRAM as system RAM. This branch gives UMA devices a per-device host buffer type (`Vulkan1_Host`) whose buffers the device owns and reads in place, so weights put there cost nothing to read on the 760M (the zero-copy decode win in your handoff 8.7). The RTX 4050 is discrete, so `*_Host` for it is the global pinned staging buffer, not readable in place. So "UMA variant" = putting Vulkan1 first in `-dev` so the `.*=CPU` weights resolve to `Vulkan1_Host`, versus putting Vulkan0 first so they land in pinned staging.

Same layers on the 760M in both, only the host buft differs: pinned `Vulkan_Host` (order B) is much faster at prefill (+23%) but much slower at decode (-44%), exactly the in-place vs staged tradeoff. That is the axis the rest of the sweep explores.

**`test_v1_share_cuda.bat`** - the Vulkan1-share hypothesis test for `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS` (47 GB, 2 parts), 11 runs, dry-run validated. Two things I found while writing it, which explain why Vulkan1 never "helped" for that model:

1. **Your `test_perf_sweep_cuda.bat` could never have run**: it passes `--lazy on`, and this build rejects it (`error: invalid argument: --lazy`); the correct flag is `--lazy-mode on` (`-lzm`). Consistent with `prompts_perf/sweep_cuda/summary.txt` not existing - that sweep produced nothing.
2. **`bench`... `CUDA0` does not exist in this build**: `build/CMakeCache.txt` has `GGML_CUDA:BOOL=OFF`, so `-dev CUDA0` -> `invalid device: CUDA0` (that's also why `-ot` only lists `CPU`, `Vulkan0`, `Vulkan1`). The new bat defaults to `DEV0=Vulkan0` (same physical 4050) and needs `-DGGML_CUDA=ON` only if you want to use CUDA0.
3. The bat also separates `--lazy-mode` per run, because with lazy mode every tensor goes to the CPU buft and `-ot`/`-ts` then only decide compute, not weight placement - so a "weights resident on Vulkan1" test is meaningless under lazy mode.

One cmd landmine worth knowing (documented in the md): with top-level `call :run` lines, this file made cmd skip the first run, run phases out of order and execute two phases twice. Moving the calls inside the `for` block (like all your older sweeps do) fixed it; the trace confirmed it.

- path: test_v1_share_cuda.bat
  content: |
      @echo off
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      rem does giving Vulkan1 a slice of the big model help the main device?
      rem
      rem model   : Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS (47 GB, 2 parts)
      rem main dev: DEV0 below. CUDA0 needs a build with -DGGML_CUDA=ON, this build is
      rem           Vulkan only, so DEV0=Vulkan0 works as is (same physical RTX 4050).
      rem
      rem hypothesis: the main device streams everything, so moving even ~1 GB of layers
      rem (5-15% of 64 layers) onto the 760M frees the main device and/or lets those
      rem layers read their weights in place from Vulkan1_Host (the UMA aperture).
      rem
      rem phases:
      rem   1 baseline and the "Vulkan1 listed but owns 0 layers" control
      rem   2 Vulkan1 share 5/8/15%, main device first
      rem   3 same shares with Vulkan1 first (Vulkan1 owns the FIRST layers)
      rem   4 draft on Vulkan1, frees main device VRAM and gives Vulkan1 the draft work
      rem   5 no lazy mode, weights in a host buft, Vulkan1 reads its layers in place
      rem
      rem lazy mode: with --lazy-mode on every tensor is lazy and the loader sends it to the
      rem CPU buft, so -ot and the layer share only decide compute, not weight placement.
      rem phase 5 drops it so the weights are placed by the split / by -ot.
      rem
      rem tags: b0 = baseline, c0 = control 0 layers, s<share> = Vulkan1 share in percent,
      rem       r = Vulkan1 listed first, d1 = MTP draft on Vulkan1, h = host buft weights
      rem
      rem logs: prompts_perf\sweep_v1\<tag>_b<ub>.log
      rem summary CSV: prompts_perf\sweep_v1\summary.txt
      rem ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
      setlocal enabledelayedexpansion
      taskkill /F /IM llama-server.exe /T >nul 2>&1
      ping -n 9 127.0.0.1 >nul
      
      set BIN=D:\shared\project\llama.cpp\build\bin
      set M=D:\shared\ai-models\IQ3_XXS\Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_XXS-00001-of-00002.gguf
      set PDIR=D:\shared\project\llama.cpp\prompts_perf
      set OUT=%PDIR%\sweep_v1
      if not exist "%OUT%" mkdir "%OUT%"
      set SUM=%OUT%\summary.txt
      rem the summary is kept between invocations so an interrupted sweep can be resumed
      if not exist "%SUM%" echo tag,dev_order,ts,main_dev,b,ub,extra,prompt_tps,gen_tps > "%SUM%"
      
      set DEV0=Vulkan0
      set C=20000
      set U=2048
      set LZ=--lazy-mode on
      set HOST=-ot ".*=CPU"
      
      rem --lazy-mode is the correct flag, "--lazy on" is rejected
      set COMMON=-m %M% --load-mode none -fitt 800MB ^
       --spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-type-k q4_1 --spec-draft-type-v q4_1 --spec-draft-n-max 3 ^
       -fa on -ctk q4_1 -ctv q4_1 -t 6 -tb 6 -np 1 --cache-ram 0 ^
       --chat-template-file "D:\shared\ai-models\chat_template.jinja" ^
       --reasoning on --reasoning-format deepseek --temp 0.3 --min-p 0.05 --top-p 0.95 --top-k 40 ^
       -n 4 -lv 5
      
      rem runs stay inside the for block on purpose: cmd mis-resumes after a top level call :run
      for %%X in (1) do (
          echo === phase 1: baseline, no Vulkan1 listed ===
          call :run b0     "%DEV0%"         "100"   %DEV0% "%U%" "" "%LZ%" ""
      
          echo === phase 2: Vulkan1 share, main device first ===
          call :run c0     "%DEV0%,Vulkan1" "100,0" %DEV0% "%U%" "" "%LZ%" ""
          call :run s5     "%DEV0%,Vulkan1" "95,5"  %DEV0% "%U%" "" "%LZ%" ""
          call :run s8     "%DEV0%,Vulkan1" "92,8"  %DEV0% "%U%" "" "%LZ%" ""
          call :run s15    "%DEV0%,Vulkan1" "85,15" %DEV0% "%U%" "" "%LZ%" ""
      
          echo === phase 3: Vulkan1 first, it owns the first layers ===
          call :run s5r    "Vulkan1,%DEV0%" "5,95"  %DEV0% "%U%" "" "%LZ%" ""
          call :run s8r    "Vulkan1,%DEV0%" "8,92"  %DEV0% "%U%" "" "%LZ%" ""
      
          echo === phase 4: MTP draft on Vulkan1 ===
          call :run s8d1   "%DEV0%,Vulkan1" "92,8"  %DEV0% "%U%" "" "%LZ%" "--spec-draft-device Vulkan1"
          call :run s15d1  "%DEV0%,Vulkan1" "85,15" %DEV0% "%U%" "" "%LZ%" "--spec-draft-device Vulkan1"
      
          echo === phase 5: no lazy mode, weights in a host buft ===
          rem needs the weights in host RAM (47 GB), drop these two runs if that does not fit
          call :run s8h    "Vulkan1,%DEV0%" "8,92"  %DEV0% "%U%" "%HOST%" "" ""
          call :run s8hb   "%DEV0%,Vulkan1" "92,8"  %DEV0% "%U%" "%HOST%" "" ""
      )
      
      echo.
      echo === sweep done, summary:
      type "%SUM%"
      goto :eof
      
      :run
      set TAG=%~1
      rem resume: a tag that already has a row is done, skip it
      findstr /B /C:"%TAG%," "%SUM%" >nul 2>&1
      if not errorlevel 1 (
          echo %TAG% already in summary, skipping
          goto :eof
      )
      set DEV=%~2
      set TS=%~3
      set MDEV=%~4
      set B=%~5
      set OT=%~6
      set LAZY=%~7
      set EXTRA=%~8
      set DEVQ=%DEV:,=+%
      set TSQ=%TS:,=+%
      set LOG=%OUT%\%TAG%_b%B%.log
      echo ============================================================
      echo %TAG% dev=%DEV% ts=%TS% main=%MDEV% b=%B% ub=%B% c=%C% ot=%OT% lazy=%LAZY% extra=%EXTRA%
      taskkill /F /IM llama-server.exe /T >nul 2>&1
      ping -n 6 127.0.0.1 >nul
      "%BIN%\llama-cli.exe" %COMMON% -dev "%DEV%" -ts "%TS%" %LAZY% %OT% %EXTRA% -c %C% -b %B% -ub %B% -f "%PDIR%\prompt_%C%.txt" > "%LOG%" 2>&1
      echo exit=%ERRORLEVEL%
      findstr /C:"Prompt: " "%LOG%"
      rem the per device buffer sizes show where the weights landed and whether they fit
      findstr /C:"model buffer size" "%LOG%"
      findstr /C:"Vulkan1 (" "%LOG%"
      findstr /C:"offloaded" "%LOG%"
      for /f "tokens=3,7" %%a in ('findstr /C:"Prompt: " "%LOG%"') do (
          echo %TAG%,%DEVQ%,%TSQ%,%MDEV%,%B%,%B%,%EXTRA%,%%a,%%b >> "%SUM%"
          echo %TAG%,%TS%,%%a,%%b
      )
      goto :eof
      
  referencedBy: {}

All done, results in `test_v1s.md`. Summary:

**The mmap question:** `--load-mode mmap` alone does NOT fix it. Tested directly on the c0 repro - log confirms `load_mode = mmap` active, then the same Vulkan0 OOM (`test_mmap_c0.bat`, `sweep_v1/c0_mmaptest_b2048.log`). What does fix loading with Vulkan1 in `-dev`:
- `-ot ".*=CPU"` - weights in host buft, no device staging
- `--lazy-mode on --cpu-moe` - experts streamed, device buffers shrink to fit

**Sweep results** (Flash-Next, no MTP, c20000/ub2048, -st, 20k prompt):

| config | weights | prompt t/s | gen t/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| Vulkan0 alone, lazy | streamed | **194.2** | 1.5 |
| Vulkan0 alone | host buft | 176.2 | 2.9 |
| 95/5 + cpu-moe | lazy | 119.2 | 1.6 |
| 85/15 + cpu-moe | lazy | 118.2 | **4.2** |
| 95/5 | host buft | 81.6 | 1.2 |
| 85/15 | host buft | 52.7 | 0.7 |

**Conclusion:** any Vulkan1 share cuts prefill 40-70%. Cross-device pipes between the 4050 and the 760M eat the capacity win. Only reason to split is decode (85/15+cpu-moe = 2.8x gen t/s). Recommendation for the big model: `-dev Vulkan0 --lazy-mode on`, no split. Plain lazy + share without cpu-moe still OOMs (s5l/s15l failed) - cpu-moe is the required ingredient.

**CUDA0,Vulkan1:** this build has `GGML_CUDA=OFF`, so I used Vulkan0 (same physical 4050) as the stand-in. Section 4 of test_v1s.md has the one-line change (`set DEV0=CUDA0`) to rerun after a CUDA rebuild. Also confirmed your `-fitt` report: it aborts with "tensor_split already set by user" whenever Vulkan1 is in `-dev`, it never engaged in any run.

Housekeeping: the hung llama-cli (6.9 GB, missing `-st`, my fault from the gemma dry-run) is gone, and `test_v1s_split.bat` now hardcodes `-st` so it can't hang again.
